newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty weakens vs basket in live trade, depos up.
newsitem.headline: Zloty weakens vs basket in live trade, depos up.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the basket of currencies after a lively session amid speculative transactions tracking dollar/mark moves and small scale foreign sales of Polish T-bills, dealers said.

They said that Tuesday's U.S. federal reserve decision to raise the base rate did not have any major effect on the Polish market because foreign investors did not have any substantial Polish positions.
"The zloty mirrored dollar/mark swings and foreign sales of T-bills were small, as they had been already cut before," said Wlodzimierz Kado from Bank Handlowy SA.

The zloty closed at 2.97/2.94 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Tuesday's 3.03/3.02 percent. It closed at 3.0865/75 to the dollar, down from 3.0785/95 on Tuesday and at 1.8240/45 to the mark against 1.8240/49.

Dealers said that small T-bill sales might have come from adjustments in medium term investors' portfolios, but expected renewed buying on zloty rise expectations if the Polish currency eases to some 2.8 percent from the parity rate.
"Foreigners may start some speculative purchases of Polish paper when the zloty is around 2.8 percent from parity," a dealer at a major Polish bank said.

The secondary T-bill market livened up on Wednesday with focus on short 40-days-to-maturity paper quoted 0.2 point higher from Tuesday at 21.30/21.10 percent against the 8-week primary average yield of 21.39 percent.
The benchmark 52-week paper was quoted flat at 21.55/21.45 percent against the primary average yield of 21.43 percent.

Short-term deposit rates rose as banks borrowed more funds to protect positions ahead of the last working day of March's reserve period on Friday and one-week deposits were at 23.10 percent signalling liquidity problems may continue.
The monthly period of averaging reserve accounts ends during the Easter holiday break on Monday, which forces banks to square positions earlier.

"The last working day of the reserve period is Friday, but the reserve itself ends on Monday, which is unconvenient for banks as any negative balance left multiplies over the long weekend," said a dealer at a foreign bank here.
Overnight rates were quoted at 23.10/23.30 percent, up from 22.55/22.75 pct at opening, tomorrow/next rates were at 23.15/23.35 percent, up from opening's 22.80/23.30 percent.
